---
title: "Catalogue structure"
subtitle: "Standard fields for documenting each assessment method"
---

Alongside the hierarchy, every method gets a **standardised catalogue entry**. The catalogue does more than list methods: it guides their responsible use by documenting data needs, pre-processing requirements, model assumptions, sensitivities, **misuse prevention** (when not to use a method, common misuses, a pre-use checklist and advice suitability) and the implementation resources available.

::: {.catalogue-wrap}
::: {.catalogue-grid}
::: {.catalogue-card}
### Catalogue of assessment methods

- Method families with links to named methods
- Biomass dynamic and dynamic pool branches, with equilibrium per-recruit and length-based age-structured sub-classes
- Method entries that can be expanded with interactive tools
:::

::: {.catalogue-note}
**Concept:** the catalogue complements the hierarchy. It documents what each method requires, how it should be prepared and interpreted, and where a mismatch between assumptions and data is likely to cause bias.
:::
:::

## Page layout: the method pipeline

Each method page reads in the order an analyst works, following the pipeline in the toolbox concept (N. Gutierrez): **1 · Data** (requirements, method-specific data template, preparation) → **2 · Method** (software or app, settings, assumptions) → **3 · Outputs** (diagnostics and sensitivity demos), with **use and misuse** guidance and **case studies** alongside. Every step has its own guidance. The standard fields below are grouped into these steps; the *Page section* column shows where each field appears.

## Standard catalogue fields

Every method page in the [catalogue](../methods/index.qmd) follows these sections and fields. The template is [`methods/_template.qmd`](https://github.com/Henning-Winker/nfifm-toolbox/blob/main/methods/_template.qmd).

```{r}
#| echo: false
source("R/toolbox.R")
DT::datatable(read_catalogue_fields(), rownames = FALSE, filter = "top",
              options = list(pageLength = 30, dom = "t", scrollX = TRUE),
              class = "compact stripe hover")
```
